title: Kalmia Latifolia
text:
Kalmia Latifolia.

         Mountain Laurel. (Ericaceae.)



Adapted to acute neuralgia, rheumatism, gouty complaints, especially when
        heart is involved as a sequel of rheumatism or gout. In heart diseases that have developed
        from rheumatism, or alternate with it. Pains sticking, darting, pressing,   shooting in a downward direction   (Cac. - upward, Led.);
        attended or succeeded by   numbness of affected part
        (Acon., Cham., Plat.). Severe stitching pain in right eye and orbit (left eye, Spig.);
        stiffness in muscles, pain < when turning the eyes (Spig.); begins at sunrise, < at
        noon and leaves at sunset (Nat. m.). Rheumatism: pains intense, change places suddenly going
        from joint to joint; joint hot, red, swollen; worse from least movement. Vertigo when
        stooping or looking down (Spig.). Pulse slow, scarcely perceptible (35 to 40 per minute);
        pale face and cold extremities.


  Relations  . - Similar: to, Led.,
        Rhod., Spig., in rheumatic affections and gout. It follows Spig. well in heart disease.



 Keynotes  by H.C. Allen
